text:
laura_support: Customer reported streaming response truncates after rejoin. They see JSON that ends with an open array like "[ {"choice": "..." }," and then the connection closes. finish_reason is absent. They supplied a curl repro and HAR.

mike_runtime: Can you paste the curl? Also need model, protocol (http/2 or http/1.1) and if there's a proxy in front.

laura_support: Repro: ```curl -v -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=rw-large" -d '{"prompt":"long-story","stream":true}'``` They are on http/2 via our edge, using a corporate proxy. Happened after they reconnected (client resumed with range header). HAR attached in ticket.

sasha_oncall: Deploy-bot shows no error at LB level for that timeframe. @deploy-bot any connection resets?
deploy-bot: LB: 2024-11-15T16:10:11Z conn reset from upstream; proxy-id=gw-12, req_id=rdw-8f2a9. No 5xx returned to client.

mike_runtime: Two hypotheses: (1) proxy is trimming last bytes on resume and leaving a trailing comma/open array fragment, (2) our resume logic emits an empty sentinel but proxy drops it. Can you confirm if the client used resume headers or simply reopened a new stream?

laura_support: Customer says client re-opened using same session token and sent a custom "resume-offset" header with last-event-id. They saw entire stream up to the fragment, then EOF. They also tried with a simple reconnect (no resume header) and got same truncation.

mike_runtime: Please ask customer for the exact response bytes (hex or raw) and any client logs. In the meantime, provide them this quick workaround: disable connection pooling in their proxy or increase idle keepalive to 90s and test. Also try forcing http/1.1 to rule out http/2 stream reset behavior.

laura_support: Sent steps. Customer returned raw payload (truncated): ```[{"id":1,"tokens":["Once"," upon" ]},{"id":2,"tokens":["a"," time"]},]``` ends there. No finish_reason field anywhere.

sasha_oncall: That payload shows a trailing comma and open array. If our runtime always emits a terminal object like {"finish_reason":"stop"} or a closing bracket, then something between us and the client is dropping final bytes. Check ingress/outgress buffer flush around proxy handoff.

mike_runtime: I pulled the request logs for req_id=rdw-8f2a9. Server side completed write of terminal frame at 2024-11-15T16:10:12.123Z (bytes_sent==len). Upstream acked. After that, we see a TCP FIN from gw-12 at +40ms. There is a replayable pattern where gw-12 aggressively resets idle streams on resume paths.

mike_runtime: Repro suggestion for eng: run a small local proxy (nginx with proxy_buffering off) between client and our edge, replay customer's curl with resume header. Capture tcpdump on both sides. Look for last FIN or RST from proxy.

laura_support: Customer tried disabling their corporate proxy and the stream completed normally (closing bracket + finish_reason). So likely an intermediary bug. They've asked if we can add a final flush/sentinel to make it more tolerant.

sasha_oncall: LC: we can add an optional keepalive sentinel ("\n--redwood-stream-end--\n") but that would break strict JSON for some clients. Alternative: emit a final zero-length SSE event or an explicit final JSON object that is small and unlikely to be dropped. Need product sign-off.

mike_runtime: Short-term: advise customers to avoid proxies that re-use or prematurely close streams for resume flows. Long-term: eng-rt to add a configurable final fence boolean flag on stream API that appends a tiny base64-signed trailing chunk after closing bracket. That preserves JSON (placed after newline) and gives clients a way to verify completeness.

laura_support: I'll update customer: they confirmed disabling proxy fixed it; they're OK with workaround for now. Filing a ticket: ENG-RT-1142 to evaluate stream sentinel design. Closing from support once eng ticket created.

sasha_oncall: Filed ENG-RT-1142 with logs and req_id=rdw-8f2a9. Assigning to @mike_runtime. Marking severity P2.

mike_runtime: Thanks. For the record: include edge gw-12 vendor/version and nginx conf snippet from customer. Also ask QA to run a flakey-proxy test harness hitting our staging streams for 24h to catch regressions.
